[related article](https://collective.flashbots.net/t/trustless-payments-and-relays/5761) 

if my understanding is correct, the advantages are mostly about widening the bidder pool and giving proposers more options

- currently, relays can accept uncollateralized or under-collateralized bids, which suits occasional builders and large one-off blocks that wouldn't justify a big in-protocol stake
-  sidecar can forward in-protocol bids to a relay or builders, which pays off for the proposer when several competing fast builders exist

I think relays will continue for the reasons you state here plus some others.

The sidecar will also likely continue. Primarily because relays and sidecars can work closely together to iterate quickly on custom endpoints and other features the node operator may want.

It functions as an adapter layer over the builder api.
